newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Convincing convergence top EMU priority - George.
newsitem.headline: Convincing convergence top EMU priority - George.

text.p: Bank of England Governor Eddie George said the key consideration for a country joining economic and monetary union (EMU) was to show convincing evidence of sustainable economic convergence.
He told reporters this was more important than the EMU timetable or a focus on individual convergence criteria.

Asked whether it would be better to delay EMU rather than admit a country which did not meet the target of capping its budget deficit at three percent of GDP, George said substantive economic convergence was the main issue.

"Unless people both in the country and in the other participant countries were persuaded that this situation (sustainable convergence) existed, then it (a delay) would be advisable in the interests of the applicant country and the other countries. That is much more important than the timetable," he said.
